# BlazorExpress.ChartJS

> BlazorExpress.ChartJS is an open-source (Apache-2.0) Blazor component library for Chart.js 4.6. Each chart type (bar, bubble, doughnut, line, pie, polar area, radar, scatter) is a Razor component whose data, datasets, options and plugins are typed C# classes. It runs in Blazor WebAssembly, Blazor Web Apps (Server and Auto render modes) and .NET MAUI Blazor Hybrid, on .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. The current version is 2.0.0.

This documentation site (https://chartjs.blazorexpress.com) is a Blazor WebAssembly app: its pages need JavaScript to render. For plain text, use this file and the raw GitHub files linked below.

Key facts:

- Install: `dotnet add package BlazorExpress.ChartJS --version 2.0.0`, then `@using BlazorExpress.ChartJS` in `_Imports.razor`.
- Scripts, at the end of `<body>` and in this order: Chart.js 4.6.1 (`https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/Chart.js/4.6.1/chart.umd.js`), chartjs-plugin-datalabels 2.2.0 only if you use data labels, then `_content/BlazorExpress.ChartJS/blazorexpress.chartjs.js`. They go in `wwwroot/index.html` (WebAssembly, MAUI) or `Components/App.razor` (Blazor Web App).
- A chart is drawn by `InitializeAsync(chartData, options)` in `OnAfterRenderAsync`, because Chart.js needs the rendered canvas. In a Blazor Web App the page needs an interactive render mode. Change data with `UpdateAsync`, `AddDataAsync` and `AddDatasetAsync`.
- Time axes (`time`, `timeseries`) need no date-adapter script: the library registers its own. Use `ChartData.TimeLabels`, `TimeData` and `ChartTimeValue` (`DateOnly`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`). Do not add `chartjs-adapter-date-fns` or luxon.
- Options that Chart.js takes as a JavaScript function: register the function in your own script loaded after `blazorexpress.chartjs.js` with `blazorexpress.chartjs.registerFunction('name', fn)`, then reference it from C# with `new ChartFunction("name")`. Names are looked up only in that registry, never evaluated as code.
- 2.0.0 changes some defaults compared with 1.x (radar and bubble axes start at zero, data-label styles, hidden datasets stay hidden after `UpdateAsync`, animated updates). Read the breaking changes before upgrading.

## Quick start

```razor
<BarChart @ref="barChart" Width="600" />

@code {
    private BarChart barChart = default!;

    protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (firstRender)
        {
            var data = new ChartData
            {
                Labels = new List<string> { "Chrome", "Firefox", "Safari", "Edge" },
                Datasets = new List<IChartDataset>
                {
                    new BarChartDataset { Label = "Visitors", Data = new List<double?> { 55000, 15000, 18000, 21000 } }
                }
            };

            await barChart.InitializeAsync(data, new BarChartOptions { Responsive = true });
        }

        await base.OnAfterRenderAsync(firstRender);
    }
}
```

- [Getting started](https://chartjs.blazorexpress.com/docs/getting-started/introduction): install, scripts, a first chart, supported versions, time axes and JavaScript functions
- [Blazor WebAssembly setup](https://chartjs.blazorexpress.com/docs/getting-started/blazor-webassembly-net-8): step-by-step guide
